title: Heaps, top-k and merging streams

objectives.text: Maintain a min-heap or bounded top-k invariant without treating its array as fully sorted.
Merge sorted streams using one current head per stream and an explicit equal-key ordering rule.
Release all ended half-open sessions using an active-end heap.
Prove minimum rooms equals maximum simultaneous depth and preserve peak rather than final occupancy.
Separate frequency counting from top-k numeric-value selection.
Maintain worst-kept heap root with correct tie direction and sort only final retained entries.
Emit the k-th largest after every prefix using one persistent bounded heap, including duplicate values and insufficient-prefix sentinels.
Maintain an ordered lower/upper partition with balanced heaps and emit exact integer or half-integer prefix medians.

blocks.markdown: A binary min-heap stores a partial order. In the zero-based array representation, each parent at i is no greater than its existing children at 2*i+1 and 2*i+2. This makes index 0 the minimum, but it does not sort siblings or the entire backing array. heapify restores this invariant in-place; heappush adds and heappop removes the minimum while restoring it. Use the heap operations rather than mutate an arbitrary entry and assume the invariant survives.

blocks.source:
import heapq
heap = [5, 1, 4, 2]
heapq.heapify(heap)
print(heap[0])
print([heapq.heappop(heap) for _ in range(4)])
try:
    heapq.heappop(heap)
except IndexError:
    print("empty heap")
blocks.caption: Expected output: 1, then [1, 2, 4, 5], then empty heap. Repeated pops produce sorted output, but the intermediate backing list need not be sorted. The empty pop raises IndexError under the library contract.

blocks.markdown: Under unit-cost comparisons, pushing/popping a binary heap moves along its logarithmic height. Building a heap bottom-up with heapify takes O(n) work; it is not n independent logarithmic pushes. The rough height-count argument sums many leaves requiring no downward movement, half as many possible parents requiring one level, and successively fewer high-level nodes. The total is bounded by a constant multiple of n. Copies, expensive comparisons and allocations remain part of a real cost model.

To retain the k largest VALUES including multiplicity, keep a min-heap of at most k observations. After each prefix it contains that prefix's min(k,prefix_length) largest values as a multiset. Once full, its root is the smallest retained value. A new value no larger than the root need not replace anything; a larger one replaces the root. Equal values are interchangeable in this value-only contract, but not necessarily when identity or arrival order matters. k=0 returns no retained values.

blocks.caption: Expected output: [8, 5, 5], then [2, 1], then []. Duplicates count as separate observations here. The final sort is needed because the heap is not fully ordered. This is not the same as top-k DISTINCT SYMBOLS by frequency, which first needs counting and a different rank/tie contract.

blocks.markdown: For n observations and k>0, bounded retention uses O(k) retained storage and O(n log(k+1)) worst-case heap comparison work under this simple bound, plus O(k log(k+1)) to return a fully ordered result when k<=n. An implementation also has to handle k>n by retaining only n values. Returning a generator can avoid materialising a whole merged output, but does not remove the caller's storage if the caller wraps it in list.

For k sorted ascending streams, the next global minimum must be one of the current stream heads. Put one head per nonempty stream in a min-heap. Pop the smallest head, emit it, and replenish from that SAME stream only. All unseen values in that stream are no smaller, preserving the candidate-head invariant. The example stores (value,stream_id), so equal heads prefer smaller stream IDs. An empty stream contributes no head. None is not an allowed data value in this integer-only fixture, making it a valid exhausted-iterator sentinel.

blocks.caption: Expected output: [1, 1, 2, 4, 5]. The function yields values one at a time. Initialisation holds at most one head per input stream, and later steps replenish one. If a stream violates ascending order, this algorithm does not repair it or promise a sorted output. Its deterministic equal-head rule follows stream_id, not a real venue sequence.

blocks.markdown: Heap tuples compare lexicographically. A (priority,payload) pair can try to compare payloads when priorities tie, causing an error for unordered objects such as dictionaries. Add a unique monotonic sequence number before the payload: (priority,sequence,payload). That implements FIFO among equal priorities under this explicitly chosen rule and prevents payload comparison. If priorities change, pushing a new entry does not delete an older entry automatically; stale-entry/version handling needs another explicit policy.

blocks.source:
import heapq
heap = []
heapq.heappush(heap, (2, 0, {"id": "A"}))
heapq.heappush(heap, (2, 1, {"id": "B"}))
print(heapq.heappop(heap)[2]["id"])
print(heapq.heappop(heap)[2]["id"])
blocks.caption: Expected output: A, then B. Equal priority 2 is resolved by the unique sequence 0 before 1, not by comparing dictionary payloads. The sequence is local insertion evidence, not authenticated exchange chronology.

blocks.markdown: Independent transfer: compare retained top-k values with a full descending sort on small lists, including duplicates, k=0, k>n and empty input. Merge several sorted finite streams and compare to sorting their concatenation; include ties and empty streams. Deliberately violate sorted input and describe why the candidate-head proof fails. State priority direction, output ordering, tie rule, payload comparison and stale-entry behavior before calling a heap a complete scheduler.

Technical reference: [Python heapq](https://docs.python.org/3/library/heapq.html) for heap ordering, heapify, sorted merging and priority-queue tie handling. This Python3.12-compatible example uses only the min-heap API; newer max-heap helper APIs are not assumed available. No production scheduler, concurrent queue or C++ implementation is claimed.

Host all sessions

Source:1..100000 positive-duration half-open intervals [s,e),0<=s<e<=1e9. Cannot discard a session. rooms_needed(intervals) returns a one-line list with minimum capacity, not a maximum selectable subset. End t may share a room with start t. Use the earlier heap root/pop/push semantics; active entries are END times, not room IDs.

Active-set invariant

Process by nondecreasing(start,end). For start s, pop WHILE minimum end<=s. Equal endings are released first. When root>s, all retained ends>s; their starts were already processed, so every retained session is active at s. Push the new end and save maximum heap size. Final size can be less than the earlier peak. A single pop does not remove every finished session in an active-set representation.

Depth lower and upper bounds

At a time with d simultaneous sessions, any valid assignment needs d rooms. Conversely process starts and reuse any room whose prior interval ended, opening a room only if all existing rooms are occupied. Opening room d witnesses d intervals overlapping at this start. Thus the constructive assignment never exceeds maximum depth, which is already a lower bound. This heap computes depth but does not return the assignment itself.

Trace,work,transfer

For[(0,3),(1,2),(2,4),(4,5)], sizes after releases/push are1,2,2,1. Answer2, not final1. Release end2 before start2. Independently sort events with endings before equal starts, or count s<=t<e at every start time. Include duplicates,nesting,touching and max100000 intervals. Sorting and heap operations cost O(n log n), storage O(n) in the worst case; capacity<=n.

blocks.caption: Expected ['2'], ['1']. Complete Python3.12 list-lines peak-depth implementation. No room-ID assignment or production capacity promise.

Different from largest values

Source:1..200000 integers with |value|<=1e9 and1<=k<=n. Report up to k DISTINCT values by count descending,then value ascending. Return list of strings "value count". A heap of largest input values ignores frequency and is not a solution. First count using a dictionary; m distinct keys have positive counts summing to n. Repeated sightings increase a count,not the number of candidate keys.

Quality key and heap invariant

Define quality=(count,-value):larger means better. Higher count wins;equal count prefers smaller value,whose negative is larger. A min-heap then exposes the WORST retained key. While heap has fewer than k,insert. Otherwise replace root only if new quality>root. Inductively the heap contains the best min(k,keys_seen) candidates: an inferior new key cannot displace any of them; a superior key displaces exactly the current worst. Unique values make the total quality ordering deterministic.

Membership is not output order

Heap layout is not sorted. Sort the retained qualities reverse=True to get count descending and -value descending,which is value ascending. Convert back with value=-neg_value. For [5,3,5,1,3,5,3,9],k2,keys3and5bothcount3:report3 3 then5 3. With same-frequency values1and9 andk1,1wins. Using(count,value)would evict the smaller value incorrectly. Counter.most_common breaks equal counts by first appearance,not by numeric value;do not rely on that API to satisfy this contract.

Resources and independent transfer

Counting costs expected O(n) with Python dictionary assumptions,not unconditional worst-case hashing. Heap phase O(m log(k+1)),final sort O(min(k,m)log(min(k,m)+1));space O(m+k) plus returned text. If k>m,report m entries. Sorting all m by(-count,value)is a simpler O(m log m)valid baseline,and an independent output oracle. Test input-permutation invariance,ties,negative IDs,high-frequency small values versus rare large ones,k1,k=n,and200000distinct keys. This final-frequency design is not an online continually-updated top-k service.

From final top-k to every prefix

The existing min-heap retains the min(k,prefix_length) largest observations as a multiset. The task asks for the root after EACH insertion once k observations exist, not a final sorted list. Keep the same heap between arrivals. Rebuilding or sorting every prefix would abandon the O(n log k) target.

Root and multiplicity proof

While len(heap)<k, push every value and print -1 until the heap reaches k. Once full, a value greater than the root replaces it; a smaller or equal value can be ignored because it cannot increase the k-th largest value. Equal observations still count separately while filling the heap. A full heap root is exactly the smallest of the k retained values, hence rank k.

Trace and limits

For k=2 and stream [5,5,3,8], output -1,5,5,5. A true k-th value of -1 is numerically indistinguishable from the warm-up sentinel, as the public contract permits. k=1 is a running maximum; k=n emits -1 until the final minimum. n<=200000 and negative inputs are valid. Heap storage is O(k), output O(n); no identity ordering or distinct-values rule is implied.

Partition and size invariants

Keep the lower half in a max-heap represented by negated values, and the upper half in a normal min-heap. Every lower value must be <= every upper value. Keep len(lower)==len(upper) or len(lower)==len(upper)+1. The lower root is the largest lower value; the upper root is the smallest upper value. These are the middle observation(s), not arbitrary heap-array positions.

Insert, rebalance, and prove the median

Route a new price to lower if it is no greater than the lower root, otherwise to upper. This preserves partition order. If lower grows two larger, move its maximum to upper; if upper grows larger, move its minimum to lower. Moving a boundary element preserves order and fixes sizes with at most one transfer. For odd prefix length the median is the lower root; for even length it is the mean of the two roots. Duplicates remain separate observations.

Exact half units and cost

Prices are positive integers<=1000000000. Compute twice_median as 2*lower_root for odd prefixes or lower_root+upper_root for even prefixes, then print quotient//2 and decimal digit 0 or 5 according to parity. No rounding is needed. For [5, 2, 8, 2], outputs 5.0, 3.5, 5.0, 3.5. O(n log n) heap work, O(n) state/output for n<=200000. This running median stores all history; it is not a sliding-window median or constant-memory estimate.

summary: A heap exposes an extreme, not full sorted order. Bounded top-k needs an explicit multiset/rank contract; sorted stream merging needs one eligible head per stream. Keep tie/payload/stale-entry policy visible. Extension: active room depth. Extension: frequency heap order. Practice transfer: prefix kth stream. Practice transfer: balanced prefix median.
